punchline: To the owners Pollard was unlucky, to the islanders a nobody, and to Melville the most impressive man he ever met.
thirty_sec: After the Essex sank, Captain George Pollard sailed again, and his second ship, the Two Brothers, was lost in 1823. He said no owner would trust an unlucky man with a whaler again, and none did. He spent his remaining years as a night watchman on Nantucket and died in 1870. Herman Melville saw him there and wrote in his copy of Owen Chase's narrative that to the islanders Pollard was a nobody, but to him the most impressive man he had met.
